Authorize individual customer accounts via OAuth on their own Forgejo instance, retaining the instance base URL as a user input

guide.summary: Forgejo documents an OAuth2 Authorization Code provider (with PKCE) on each instance, but OAuth2 scopes are not implemented. A token can act as the user for any action, so read-only behavior must be enforced by the app.
guide.recommendation: The requested access is documented. Follow the saved setup steps and run each representative API test; execution has not been verified.

findings.title: Authorization Code grant with PKCE; no OAuth scopes
findings.detail: Forgejo supports only the Authorization Code Grant (with PKCE and OIDC). Endpoints are /login/oauth/authorize and /login/oauth/access_token on the customer's instance, so the base URL must be kept as a user input. Scopes are not implemented, and tokens can execute any action on behalf of the user. The app must itself restrict calls to read-only.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects a user account on their own Forgejo instance.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to

findings.title: Register an OAuth2 application and redirect URI
findings.detail: An application must be registered under Settings > Applications (/user/settings/applications) to get a client ID. Confidential clients use a client secret; public clients use PKCE. The redirect URI in the token request must match the authorize request. Docs also mention instance-wide apps created at /admin/applications.
findings.appliesWhen: Before the first OAuth test on a given instance.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.
Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

findings.title: Token acts with the user's own access, incl. admin rights
findings.detail: Third-party apps obtaining a token via an application have administrative rights, and the token acts as the user. Visibility of repositories therefore follows the connected person's existing account access. Use Authorization: Bearer with the access token.
findings.appliesWhen: When listing repositories for a connected person.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.
OAuth2 Provider Access tokens obtained from Forgejo’s OAuth2 provider are accepted by these methods:
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.

findings.title: Paginated listing via GET /api/v1/user/repos
findings.detail: GET /api/v1/user/repos accepts page and limit, and the response has name per item. Pagination uses page and limit plus a Link header and x-total-count. Maximum page size is available from /api/v1/settings/api. The endpoint's summary says it lists repos the user owns, so visible-but-not-owned repos may need /repos/search.

evidence.quote: ## GET /api/v1/user/repos | List the repos that the authenticated user owns
Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
The default and maximum values for the page parameter can be obtained from the https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/settings/api endpoint.

steps.title: Register a public OAuth2 application on the customer's Forgejo instance
steps.detail: Prepare (not executed here): on <INSTANCE_BASE_URL> open /user/settings/applications and create an OAuth2 application registered as a PUBLIC client (PKCE, no client secret). Add one redirect URI of your app. Record the Client ID. Forgejo OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token acts as the user; read-only behavior is enforced by this app only.
steps.doneWhen: A public OAuth2 application exists and its Client ID and exact redirect URI are recorded. If the registration UI is unavailable on the instance, an instance restriction may apply.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .
Note Please ensure you have registered your OAuth application as a public client.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: full HTTPS origin supplied by the customer for their own instance
CLIENT_ID: shown after the application is created
REDIRECT_URI: exact URI configured on the application

steps.title: Prepare PKCE code_verifier, code_challenge and state
steps.detail: Generate a random code_verifier of 43-128 characters (alphanumerics, -, ., _, ~). Derive code_challenge as URL-safe base64 of SHA256(code_verifier) with code_challenge_method=S256. Generate a random state for CSRF protection. Prepare only; nothing is sent.
steps.doneWhen: CODE_VERIFIER, CODE_CHALLENGE and STATE values are generated and stored for the consent step.

evidence.quote: To achieve this, you have to provide a code_verifier for every authorization request. A code_verifier has to be a random string with a minimum length of 43 characters and a
If you have the required functionality on your client, set code_challenge to be a URL-safe base64-encoded string of the SHA256 hash of code_verifier . In that case, your code_challenge_method becomes

https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&code_challenge_method=CODE_CHALLENGE_METHOD&code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an

fields: CODE_VERIFIER: random 43-128 char string you generate
CODE_CHALLENGE: S256 hash of CODE_VERIFIER, base64url
STATE: random string you generate

steps.title: Send the person to the consent page and check the callback
steps.detail: Redirect the user's browser to <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=<CLIENT_ID>&redirect_uri=<REDIRECT_URI>&response_type=code&code_challenge_method=S256&code_challenge=<CODE_CHALLENGE>&state=<STATE>. The user approves; Forgejo redirects to REDIRECT_URI?code=RETURNED_CODE&state=STATE. Verify returned state equals STATE. The user performs consent; this guide does not execute it.
steps.doneWhen: Callback contains a code and a state matching STATE; RETURNED_CODE is captured.

evidence.quote: Redirect the user to the authorization endpoint in order to get their consent for accessing the resources:

https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&code_challenge_method=CODE_CHALLENGE_METHOD&code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an
The user will now be asked to authorize your application. If they authorize it, the user will be redirected to the REDIRECT_URL , for example:

fields: RETURNED_CODE: query parameter 'code' on the callback
STATE: must match the value you generated
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: POST to the token endpoint with the PKCE fields. Public client, so no client_secret. redirect_uri must match the authorize request. Not executed by this guide.
steps.doneWhen: Response JSON contains access_token (token_type bearer, expires_in 3600) and refresh_token.

evidence.quote: https://[ REDIRECT_URI ]?code=RETURNED_CODE&state=STATE Using the provided code from the redirect, you can request a new application and refresh token. The access token endpoint accepts POST requests with application/json and
POST https://[YOUR-FORGEJO-URL]/login/oauth/access_token { "client_id" : "YOUR_CLIENT_ID" ,
"code_verifier" : "CODE_VERIFIER" }

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
CLIENT_ID: from application registration
RETURNED_CODE: from the callback
REDIRECT_URI: identical to the authorize request
CODE_VERIFIER: the value whose hash was sent as code_challenge

steps.title: Boundary check: inspect grant and read-only request log
steps.detail: Scopes are not implemented, so the token can act as the user and cannot be restricted to read-only by Forgejo. Boundary check: confirm in your outgoing request log that only GET requests are issued and never run a create/edit/delete call. Optionally call the safe read GET /api/v1/settings/api to confirm the token works and read max_response_items.
steps.doneWhen: Request log shows only GET calls; settings call returns 200 with max_response_items. Expect the app, not Forgejo, to enforce read-only behavior.

steps.title: List visible repository names, first page
steps.detail: GET /api/v1/repos/search returns repositories the connected person can access (private included by default), unlike /user/repos which lists only owned repos. Pass page=1 and limit (at most max_response_items from /api/v1/settings/api). Repository names are at $.data[].name in the response object. Read only; no create, edit or delete calls.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with a JSON object whose $.data[].name lists repository names; a Link header with rel="next" and x-total-count show whether more pages exist.

evidence.quote: ## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories
Response JSON paths for GET /api/v1/repos/search: $.data[].name (string)
Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth2 access token from the token exchange
limit: at most max_response_items from /api/v1/settings/api

steps.title: List visible repository names, next pages
steps.detail: Take the URL from the rel="next" entry of the previous response's Link header and request it unchanged, keeping the same Authorization header. Repeat with each new response's Link header, collecting $.data[].name from every page. Stop when the Link header has no rel="next" entry. Read only.
steps.doneWhen: The final response has no rel="next" link in its Link header and all pages' names have been collected.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
< link: < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search ? limit = 1 &page = 2 > ; rel = "next", < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search? limit = 1 &page = 5252 > ; rel = "last"
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.

fields: NEXT_PAGE_URL: rel="next" target from the previous Link header
ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth2 access token from the token exchange

blockers.title: Whether /user/repos covers all visible repositories is unconfirmed
blockers.resolution: Compare /api/v1/user/repos with /api/v1/repos/search results for a test account and switch endpoints if non-owned visible repos are missing.

blockers.resolution: Confirm the customer's instance allows creating an OAuth2 application in /user/settings/applications or have an admin create it.

details.title: Authorization Code grant with PKCE; no OAuth scopes
details.detail: Forgejo supports only the Authorization Code Grant (with PKCE and OIDC). Endpoints are /login/oauth/authorize and /login/oauth/access_token on the customer's instance, so the base URL must be kept as a user input. Scopes are not implemented, and tokens can execute any action on behalf of the user. The app must itself restrict calls to read-only.
details.appliesWhen: Each customer connects a user account on their own Forgejo instance.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register a public OAuth2 application on the customer's Forgejo instance
Prepare (not executed here): on <INSTANCE_BASE_URL> open /user/settings/applications and create an OAuth2 application registered as a PUBLIC client (PKCE, no client secret). Add one redirect URI of your app. Record the Client ID. Forgejo OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token acts as the user; read-only behavior is enforced by this app only.
Fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: full HTTPS origin supplied by the customer for their own instance, CLIENT_ID: shown after the application is created, REDIRECT_URI: exact URI configured on the application

Prepare PKCE code_verifier, code_challenge and state
Generate a random code_verifier of 43-128 characters (alphanumerics, -, ., _, ~). Derive code_challenge as URL-safe base64 of SHA256(code_verifier) with code_challenge_method=S256. Generate a random state for CSRF protection. Prepare only; nothing is sent.
Fields: CODE_VERIFIER: random 43-128 char string you generate, CODE_CHALLENGE: S256 hash of CODE_VERIFIER, base64url, STATE: random string you generate

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Send the person to the consent page and check the callback
Done when: Callback contains a code and a state matching STATE; RETURNED_CODE is captured.

Exchange the authorization code for an access token
Done when: Response JSON contains access_token (token_type bearer, expires_in 3600) and refresh_token.

Boundary check: inspect grant and read-only request log
Done when: Request log shows only GET calls; settings call returns 200 with max_response_items. Expect the app, not Forgejo, to enforce read-only behavior.

List visible repository names, first page
Done when: HTTP 200 with a JSON object whose $.data[].name lists repository names; a Link header with rel="next" and x-total-count show whether more pages exist.

List visible repository names, next pages
Done when: The final response has no rel="next" link in its Link header and all pages' names have been collected.
